title: Rung 6 -- the same placement through a matrix, decided against rung 5 and not against Cycles

criterion.says: our own generated fixture -- a node's `matrix` and its TRS spelling of one placement, which must land in the same pixels

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (doc/requirements.md I.26.14). Three cubes, so E = 18 against 3, and none of the eighteen is rational at any roll. The case's real claim -- that a matrix node and its TRS twin land in identical pixels -- is exact already and needs no oracle at all.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of doc/requirements.md I.26.10 applied to this subject's own bounds: direction azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 at r = 1.54742730039249 m, and yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. The roll is -arctan(1/2) = -26.5650511771 deg, derived rather than set: for an edge of irrational raster slope the perpendicular pixel-centre offsets equidistribute over +/-0.5 px, so the smallest margin over L boundary pixels is about 0.5/L and it SHRINKS as the subject grows -- measured between 2e-5 and 1.8e-3 px here, under the oracle's own 5e-3 px jitter. For a slope p/q in lowest terms the same distance is exactly 0.5/sqrt(p^2+q^2) at every pixel centre in the plane and does not depend on L at all, and tan(45deg+t) and tan(90deg+t) stay rational whenever tan t does, so a roll of rational tangent keeps a rational silhouette rational. The previous -22.5 deg maximised edge-to-AXIS angle, which is not the quantity the comparison turns on. The SIGN is the convention src/gltf/Subject.cpp states: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. This subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so what the change buys it is a different draw of the same lottery and not exactness -- a property of the subject, and the reason its class is general-position. THE AIM IS THE BOUNDS' CENTRE (min + max) / 2 = (1.0625, 0.625, 0.0), which is what the rule aims at and what the runner recomputes: this camera declared an aim 3.5927e-3 m -- 0.435660418 px -- off it, with no derivation of its own, and re-deriving it from the rule cited here is what moved it.
camera.note: The generated subject carries no camera, so this rung's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note: A coverage rung compares a mask. The only illumination is Blender's factory world, which costs nothing to match and is left where it is.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: Emission, one colour per node, and the geometry is untouched (doc/requirements.md I.26.13). A Diffuse BSDF under a uniform environment reduces to rho*L only while no surface can be seen from another; where one can, Cycles at one sample takes ONE cosine-weighted direction per pixel and the answer is rho*L or exactly 0 -- a Bernoulli draw whose mean is the visible sky fraction, which is an ambient-occlusion estimator wearing a placement's clothes. A ShaderNodeEmission at strength 1 gathers nothing, so the world as a light, the sun's disk, a light's radius and visibility all leave at once. ONE COLOUR PER NODE because flat emission over touching bodies fuses their silhouettes: a misplaced node would hide inside the union, which is a worse instrument than the noise this replaces.

default.note: The binary mask. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe at another seed, and the whole of the emission case's acceptance. A Monte-Carlo estimator's answer depends on its seed; an emitter has no estimator, so the two dumps must agree bit for bit and any difference NAMES the integral that survived.

notes: The same chain in both spellings, and the claim is not that they are close but that they are IDENTICAL: the manifest declares translations, scales and quaternion components that are exact in binary floating point -- dyadic rationals and a quaternion of four halves, whose rotation matrix is a permutation -- so T*R*S is exact and both spellings hand the reader the same doubles. That makes this rung decidable with no oracle in it at all, and its threshold is zero disagreeing pixels rather than a tolerance. Rung 5's file is regenerated here from the same declaration rather than reached across directories, so the case stays self-describing.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the generated vertices RE-DERIVED at the aim this camera now declares: the aim was 0.435660418 px off the bounds' centre and the rule aims at the centre, so the projection moved and the fraction with it, from 0.150417386.
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. The runner recomputes it from the generated vertices and refuses a mismatch. Every triangle is counted by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this is an AREA, not a coverage.
